small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_M configs (256x128, 128x256) and BLOCK_K=16 variants to the autotune set — with KH=KW=4, stride=2 the per-parity K_par is only IC*2*2=256, so smaller K tiles with bigger M/N tiles may map better.
- Switch the output store to channels-last contiguous addressing within each program (offs_n contiguous along innermost) by tiling N as the fastest-varying dim of the store, or pre-allocate `out` in channels-last and adjust strides — current store strides OC*H_out*W_out across BLOCK_N which kills coalescing.
- Try `num_stages=2` with `num_warps=8` on the 128x128 tile; K_par=256 only needs ~4-8 K iterations so deep pipelining costs more registers than it buys.
large_guidance:
- Fuse all 4 parities into a single kernel launch: each program computes one (N, OC_tile, H_out_tile, W_out_tile) directly, iterating over all valid (kh, kw) for the *actual* output coordinate. This avoids 4 separate launches, lets the output store be fully contiguous on the W axis, and amortizes bias/epilogue work. K is small (IC*KH*KW=1024) so a single GEMM-K loop per output tile is cheap.
- Allocate output in NHWC (channels-last) and tile so BLOCK_N (OC) is the contiguous innermost dim of both load and store — the current NCHW store has BLOCK_N strided by H_out*W_out (16K floats) which is the dominant memory inefficiency.
- Consider a scatter-add formulation instead of gather: one program per (N, IC_tile, H_in_tile, W_in_tile) computes input × weight outer products and scatter-adds into output. With stride=2 there are no write conflicts across different (hi,wi) input positions when grouped by parity, and this layout reads input contiguously. Combine with epilogue fusion in a second pass, or use atomic-free scatter by per-parity grouping.
